\section{Gaussian Space --- Halfspace}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Halfspace
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Halfspace: Introduction}
Unit linear projections preserve standard Gaussian laws. Conditioning scalar rotation crossings gives an infinitesimal crossing formula and hence the normalized rotation-sensitivity limit for halfspaces.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Halfspace: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian law of a unit projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianProjection}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, sum_scaled_iid_gaussian_map}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $a=(a_i)_{i=1}^n\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfy
$\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=1$. The map $z\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^n a_i z_i$ sends the product of $n$
standard Gaussian measures on $\mathbb R$ to the standard Gaussian measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a rotated Gaussian distribution function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_rotated_gaussianCDF}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hasDerivAt_standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density. For
every $t,y\in\mathbb R$, the function
$\theta\mapsto\Phi\bigl((t-y\sin\theta)/\cos\theta\bigr)-\Phi(t)$ is differentiable at
$0$, with derivative $-\varphi(t)y$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Limit of the Gaussian CDF rotation quotient]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotated_gaussianCDF_quotient_tendsto}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_rotated_gaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF_pos}
\difficulty{4}
For all real $t$ and $y$, as $\theta$ tends to zero through positive values,
$$\frac{\left|\Phi\left(\frac{t-\sin(\theta)y}{\cos(\theta)}\right)-\Phi(t)\right|}{\theta}\longrightarrow
\varphi(t)|y|,$$ where $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ are the standard Gaussian distribution
function and density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Maximum of the standard Gaussian density]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.standardGaussianPDF_le_at_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF_eq}
\difficulty{3}
For every $x\in\mathbb R$, the standard Gaussian density satisfies
$\varphi(x)\le\varphi(0)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lipschitz bound for the Gaussian distribution function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_standardGaussianCDF_sub_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.standardGaussianPDF_le_at_zero, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hasDerivAt_standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF_pos}
\difficulty{1}
For all $x,y\in\mathbb R$, the standard Gaussian distribution function $\Phi$ satisfies
$|\Phi(x)-\Phi(y)|\le\varphi(0)|x-y|$, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian CDF rotation quotient bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotated_gaussianCDF_quotient_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_standardGaussianCDF_sub_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF_pos}
\difficulty{5}
Let $t,y\in\mathbb R$ and let $0<\theta<1$. For the standard Gaussian distribution
function $\Phi$ and density $\varphi$,
$$\frac{\left|\Phi\left(\frac{t-\sin(\theta)y}{\cos(\theta)}\right)-\Phi(t)\right|}{\theta}\le
2\varphi(0)(|t|+|y|).$$
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrated Gaussian crossing limit]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_rotated_gaussianCDF_quotient_tendsto}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotated_gaussianCDF_quotient_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotated_gaussianCDF_quotient_tendsto, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.continuous_standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and
let $\gamma$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R$. For every $t\in\mathbb R$, as
$\theta\to0$ through positive values, $\int
\frac{|\Phi((t-\sin\theta\,y)/\cos\theta)-\Phi(t)|}{\theta}\,d\gamma(y)$ tends to
$\varphi(t)\int |y|\,d\gamma(y)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian measure of differing halflines]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.standardGaussianMeasure_symmDiff_Iic}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R$ and let
$\Phi(t)=\gamma((-\infty,t])$ be its distribution function. For all $a,b\in\mathbb R$,
the Gaussian measure of the symmetric difference of the halflines $(-\infty,a]$ and
$(-\infty,b]$ is $|\Phi(b)-\Phi(a)|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First absolute Gaussian moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.integrable_id_mul_standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.integral_Iic_id_mul_standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{5}
For a real variable $y$ integrated against the standard Gaussian probability measure
$\gamma$ on $\mathbb R$, its first absolute moment is
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}|y|\,d\gamma(y)=2\varphi(0),
\]
where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Measurability of scalar rotation disagreement]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurableSet_scalar_rotation_disagreement}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every $t,\theta\in\mathbb R$, the set of $(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2$ for which exactly one
of $x\le t$ and $\cos(\theta)x+\sin(\theta)y\le t$ holds is measurable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Scalar Gaussian threshold disagreement]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.scalar_rotation_disagreement_eq_integral}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurableSet_scalar_rotation_disagreement, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.standardGaussianMeasure_symmDiff_Iic, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $t,\theta\in\mathbb R$ with $\cos\theta>0$, and let $X,Y$ be independent standard
Gaussian variables. The probability that exactly one of $X\le t$ and
$\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y\le t$ holds is $\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb
R}\left|\Phi\!\left(\frac{t-\sin\theta\,y}{\cos\theta}\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\,d\gamma(y)$,
where $\gamma$ and $\Phi$ are the standard Gaussian measure and distribution function.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Normalized scalar crossing limit]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.scalar_rotation_disagreement_quotient_tendsto}

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Scalar reduction for halfspace sensitivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_halfspace_eq_scalar}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurableSet_scalar_rotation_disagreement, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianProjection, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $a\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=1$, and let
$t,\theta\in\mathbb R$. The rotation sensitivity of the halfspace $\{z\in\mathbb
R^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i z_i\le t\}$ at angle $\theta$ equals the probability that
independent standard Gaussian scalars $U,V$ disagree on whether they are at most $t$
after the rotation: $\Pr\bigl(\neg(U\le
t\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\cos\theta\,U+\sin\theta\,V\le t)\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Infinitesimal halfspace rotation sensitivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.halfspace_rotation_quotient_tendsto}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_halfspace_eq_scalar, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.scalar_rotation_disagreement_quotient_tendsto, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{
  pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p019-b001,
  pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p019-b002
}
\difficulty{1}
For a measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and independent standard Gaussian vectors $X,Y$, put $R_A(\theta)=\Pr(1_A(X)\ne1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y))$. If $a\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfies $\sum_i a_i^2=1$ and $H=\{z:\sum_i a_i z_i\le t\}$ for $t\in\mathbb R$, then $\sqrt{\pi/2}\,R_H(\theta)/\theta\to\varphi(t)$ as $\theta\to0^+$, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absolute moment of a Gaussian linear form]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_gaussianProjection}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianProjection, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{5}
For $n\ge 0$ and coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb R$, let $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)$
have independent standard Gaussian coordinates. Then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^n}\left|\sum_{i=1}^n a_i Z_i\right|\,d\gamma_n(Z)=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n
a_i^2}\,2\varphi(0),
\]
where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $\varphi$ is the
standard Gaussian density on $\mathbb R$.
\end{lemma}
